local.headline: County Commission to vote on data center rules; Millington starts $2 ride service
body: The Shelby County Commission is set to vote on a framework for land-use rules for data centers, according to the Daily Memphian. The paper also reported that a separate ordinance could bar permits for new data centers for up to a year. State transportation officials plan to break ground on the I-55 replacement bridge project in February, the Daily Memphian reported.

FOX13 Memphis reported that Millington's on-demand ride service began Monday, with $2 trips inside city limits under a 12-month pilot. Action News 5 reported that a woman reported missing in Mississippi was found in a lake near Shelby Farms on Saturday morning. A sheriff's deputy who tried to reach her was treated for possible hypothermia, and both were taken to Regional One in non-critical condition.

Plans for I-55 bridge work at Kings' Crossing
Millington on-demand ride service launches Monday
Woman rescued from lake near Shelby Farms

state.headline: Blackburn transition team names DCS advisers; death row lawyers seek wider review
body: According to the Tennessee Lookout, Gov.-elect Marsha Blackburn's transition committee formed a four-person advisory group, chaired by former Department of Children's Services leader Jim Henry, to assess the department and recommend its future direction and leadership. Blackburn takes office Jan. 16.

WSMV reported that attorneys for death row prisoners wrote to Gov. Bill Lee and Blackburn asking for an independent review of every execution under the 2025 lethal injection protocol. Lee has paused executions through the end of 2026. The Lookout also reported that the West Tennessee Megasite Authority is considering guiding principles for data centers on land it manages outside Shelby County.

Attorneys seek wider review of execution procedures
Megasite board weighs data center principles

federal.headline: Democrats reach 258 House seats; Delta outage delays holiday travelers
body: The Associated Press, via PBS NewsHour, reported that House Democrats reached at least 258 of 435 seats on Sunday after Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx in North Carolina, as CBS News and ABC News also reported. Four races remain undecided. The new House convenes Jan. 3, 2027. ABC News reported that an outage in a Delta Air Lines weight-and-balance system delayed more than 1,600 flights on Sunday, mostly in Atlanta. Delta said it was not a hack and that systems were back to normal Sunday afternoon.

On CBS News's Face the Nation, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the government needs answers from Nvidia on whether it complied with chip export limits to China, and that he had asked for a reply within 10 days. The Hill reported Monday that Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive.

international.headline: COP31 ends without a climate deal; suspected drone strike hits Russian ship in Libya
body: UN News reported that the COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Türkiye, ended Sunday without an agreement after divisions over fossil fuels. UN Secretary-General António Guterres called the outcome "deeply disappointing." PBS NewsHour reported that countries said at the final meeting that they could not accept a draft with no fossil fuel wording. Talks move to COP32 in Addis Ababa.

CBS News, citing the Associated Press, reported that two Libyan military officials said a suspected Ukrainian drone strike damaged the Russian corvette Merkury at the Benghazi naval base. No group claimed it, and neither Russia nor Ukraine had commented at the time. UN News said the UN mission in Libya urged an investigation of attacks at the port, and that the Security Council met Monday on attacks on Ukraine's power grid and Black Sea shipping.
